clue.text: See 25
6.75 + 0.6 recurring for silky fabric

blocks.note: 6.75 is three quarters of nine, so take three of the four letters of NINE
0.6 recurring is two thirds of one, so take two of the three letters of ONE

explanation.surface: A sum producing a decimal, as if someone were calculating a price for a length of silk.
explanation.walkthrough: The numbers are fractions of number words: three quarters of NINE and two thirds of ONE, each cut from the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Ninon is a lightweight sheer fabric of silk or similar fibre, used for dresses and curtains.

clue.text: Spice added to reference book was passionately expressive?

blocks.note: a tang is a sharp, spicy flavour
the Oxford English Dictionary, the classic reference book

explanation.surface: Someone got excited when spice was added to a cookery reference book.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a playful definition: to have danced the tango, a famously passionate dance.
explanation.definitionFit: The tango is danced with dramatic, sensual intensity, so having done it is being passionately expressive in movement.

clue.text: Coe rival, yet often fastest, always showing heart?

definitions.text: Coe rival, yet often fastest, always showing heart?

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its centre, so each word in turn yields only its middle letter

blocks.note: centre of a three-letter word
centre of a five-letter word
centre of a three-letter word
centre of a five-letter word
centre of a seven-letter word

explanation.surface: A tribute to a runner who rivalled Coe and was often quickest, always running with heart.
explanation.walkthrough: Steve Ovett and Sebastian Coe were the great British middle-distance rivals of around 1980; the whole clue both describes him and spells him.
explanation.definitionFit: Steve Ovett, Olympic 800m champion in 1980, was Sebastian Coe's chief British rival on the track.

clue.text: Sparkling hospital department, highly thought of

blocks.note: A&E, accident and emergency, written without the ampersand
well regarded

explanation.surface: A lively hospital department that is well regarded by its patients.
explanation.walkthrough: A&E is the British name for the emergency room.
explanation.definitionFit: An aerated drink has gas bubbled through it, making it fizzy or sparkling.

clue.text: Piece of kit, coat on seen with a '70s jumper

indicators.note: a coat sits on the outside, so only the outer layer of letters of the following word is used

blocks.note: first and last letters
taken as written
Red Rum, the racehorse that won the Grand National steeplechase in 1973, 1974 and 1977

explanation.surface: A wardrobe item: a coat put on and worn with a seventies-style sweater.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jumper' looks like the British word for a sweater, which fits 'coat' and 'kit'; it is a horse that jumps fences.
explanation.definitionFit: A snare drum is a standard component of a drum kit, so it is one piece of the kit.

clue.text: Large group out to lunch, starter unavailable

indicators.note: the starter is the first letter, and unavailable means it is not there to use

blocks.note: barmy means crazy, as does the idiom out to lunch

explanation.surface: A big party has gone out for lunch, but the first course is off the menu.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lunch' and 'starter' set up a restaurant; the starter is the opening letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An army can mean any vast crowd or host of people, not only soldiers.

clue.text: See 25 Across
Tom dashed here?

blocks.note: surface reading: a man called Tom rushed to this place
setter's reading: the letters T, O and M are all rendered purely as dashes in a signalling system

explanation.walkthrough: In the telegraph alphabet T is one dash, O three dashes and M two, so the name is nothing but dashes.
explanation.definitionFit: The signalling alphabet of dots and dashes encodes each letter, and this name happens to need dashes only.

clue.text: A rude Etonian struggling to maintain working relations, promptly dismissed

annotation.answer: IN ONE EAR AND OUT THE OTHER

indicators.note: something struggling is thrashing about, so the letters are thrown into disorder
to maintain is to hold or keep, so the earlier letters keep the next word inside them

blocks.note: taken as written
a machine that is on is working
a bit of the other is British slang for sexual relations

explanation.surface: A boorish Old Etonian finds it hard to keep up working relationships and is quickly shown the door.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Working relations' reads as one phrase but splits: working is ON, relations is the slang 'the other', meaning sex.
explanation.definitionFit: Advice that goes in one ear and out the other is heard but instantly ignored, so it is promptly dismissed.

clue.text: On ship heading for Africa, in the doldrums reportedly?

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter
reportedly means as heard said, so we want a word that is only pronounced like the meaning

blocks.note: first letter
to be in the doldrums is to be listless or fed up

explanation.surface: A sailing ship bound for Africa lies becalmed in the doldrums near the equator.
explanation.walkthrough: The doldrums are the windless belt where ships stall, which suits the sea scene; here the phrase means bored.
explanation.definitionFit: To be aboard is to be on a ship, as a passenger or crew member.

clue.text: See 8
See 8
Cook passed quarterdeck?

indicators.note: to cook something is to work it into a new form, so these letters are reworked

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Captain Cook walked past the quarterdeck of his ship.
explanation.walkthrough: A quarterdeck is part of a ship, but read as quarter of a deck it means one of the four suits in a pack of cards.
explanation.definitionFit: Spades is one of the four suits, so it is a quarter of a deck of playing cards.

clue.text: More Italian mafiosi initially surrounding airport, dangerous element?

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of the word it follows
surrounding means going around another piece, which then sits inside

blocks.note: più is Italian for more, familiar from musical directions
Luton is an airport north of London
first letter

explanation.surface: More Italian gangsters gathering around an airport with something hazardous to smuggle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Italian' looks like it describes the mafiosi; it actually turns 'More' into Italian. Luton is a town and airport just north of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Plutonium is a radioactive, highly toxic metallic element used in nuclear weapons.

clue.text: Names European Community provided filed by operatives

indicators.note: papers filed by someone are put away inside their keeping, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: standard abbreviation
provided that means if
secret agents are operatives

explanation.surface: Spies file a report naming a European body, with a condition attached.
explanation.definitionFit: To name something precisely is to specify it, so names here is the verb.

clue.text: Comparative amount fed to horse all the time

definitions.note: the noun duration stands for the whole span, as in 'for the duration'

indicators.note: food fed to an animal goes inside it, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: a dun is a greyish-brown horse
a ratio compares two quantities

explanation.surface: A measured portion of feed given to a horse round the clock.
explanation.definitionFit: Duration is the entire time something lasts, so 'for the duration' means all the time.

clue.text: Allotment 21 gone to seed

indicators.note: something gone to seed has run wild and lost its order, so the letters are scrambled

blocks.note: the answer to clue 21

explanation.surface: An allotment, a rented vegetable plot, has been left to run to seed.
explanation.walkthrough: An allotment in Britain is a small rented garden plot, which makes 'gone to seed' look natural.
explanation.definitionFit: A quotient can mean a share or portion allotted to someone, as an allotment is.

clue.text: Alcoholic drink, beverage inspiring old writer briefly

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the last letter is dropped
to inspire is literally to breathe in, so one piece is taken inside another

blocks.note: a common beverage
a quill pen, the writing tool of old

explanation.surface: A boozy drink that once inspired an elderly author, though only for a short while.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old writer' suggests an author, but it is the instrument he wrote with.
explanation.definitionFit: Tequila is a Mexican spirit distilled from the blue agave plant.

clue.text: Case of Agincourt in place identified as scene of action

indicators.note: a case is the outside casing, so just the outer letters are wanted
in places one piece within another

blocks.note: pointing at a spot and saying 'there!' identifies a place
first and last letters

explanation.surface: Agincourt, the 1415 battle, identified as the site of the fighting.
explanation.walkthrough: Agincourt is the famous battlefield of Henry V, so 'scene of action' reads naturally as a battle site.
explanation.definitionFit: A theatre of war or operations is the area where military action takes place.

clue.text: See 22 Down
Flag featuring leader in Rome on me, old warship

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter
a thing featuring something includes it within

blocks.note: to flag is to tire or weaken
first letter
taken as written

explanation.surface: A banner bearing the initial of Rome flies over the speaker on an ancient galley.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flag' looks like a banner, fitting the warship, but it is the verb meaning to weaken; 'on' places the last piece after it in a down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A trireme was an ancient Greek or Roman galley with three banks of oars, used in naval warfare.

clue.text: Letter about surrender, as near as dammit?

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece wraps another

blocks.note: a note is a short letter
to quit is to give up

explanation.surface: A letter about giving up, which very nearly says it all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As near as dammit' is a British idiom for almost but not exactly.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases describe something almost achieved but falling just short.

clue.text: Abscess: one in five say, drained

indicators.note: drained means emptied, so the inside letters go and only the shell remains

blocks.note: a quin is one of quintuplets, five babies born together
first and last letters

explanation.surface: A medical note: one patient in five, for example, has an abscess that was drained.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drained' suits an abscess, which doctors do drain, but here it empties a word.
explanation.definitionFit: Quinsy is a peritonsillar abscess, a pus-filled swelling beside the tonsil.

clue.text: Consort, German essentially?

blocks.note: first meaning: the title of a ... consort's later life, as with Elizabeth, wife of George VI
second meaning, read backwards as wordplay

explanation.walkthrough: The second half is reverse wordplay: strip German of its outer letters and you are left with ER, the Queen, plus MA, mother. ER is the crossword label for Elizabeth Regina.
explanation.definitionFit: The Queen Mother had been queen consort to George VI before her daughter took the throne.

clue.text: Ogre: call to have one evicted

indicators.note: an evicted tenant is thrown out, so one letter is put out of the word

blocks.note: a shriek is a loud cry
Roman numeral for one, which is removed

explanation.surface: An ogre yells to get someone thrown out of his swamp.
explanation.walkthrough: The film ogre famously wants intruders evicted from his swamp, so the surface fits him well.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrek is the green ogre of the DreamWorks animated films.

clue.text: No frills on trip west of small Italian port

indicators.note: frills are trimmings on the edges, so taking them off leaves only the middle
in an across answer west means to the left, so this piece is written first

blocks.note: the inner letters
mini means small

explanation.surface: A budget trip to a small Italian resort with no extras.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No frills' suggests a budget airline flight, but it trims a word.
explanation.definitionFit: Rimini is a resort city and port on Italy's Adriatic coast.

clue.text: What can't be said of a palindrome, for sure

annotation.answer: THERE ARE NO TWO WAYS ABOUT IT

definitions.text: What can't be said of a palindrome

blocks.clueFragment: What can't be said of a palindrome
blocks.note: a palindrome reads the same in two directions
second meaning: the everyday phrase for something beyond doubt

explanation.surface: A grammarian ponders what remark would be false if applied to a palindrome, insisting on it firmly.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half is a witty, literal reading of the idiom: a palindrome can be read forwards and backwards, which is exactly two ways.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom is used to stress certainty, meaning there is no doubt or alternative view.

clue.text: Book horrifying production company, extremes trimmed back

indicators.note: trimming the extremes cuts off both end letters
back means the letters are read the other way

blocks.note: Hammer Films, the British studio famous for horror movies

explanation.surface: A novel is put out by a horror film studio, with its edges cut back.
explanation.walkthrough: Hammer was the British studio behind classic Dracula and Frankenstein films.
explanation.definitionFit: Emma is Jane Austen's 1815 novel, so it is a book by title.

clue.text: American author in German vessel on water

blocks.note: a stein is a German beer mug
a beck is a northern English word for a stream

explanation.surface: An American writer is aboard a German ship at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' suggests a boat, fitting 'on water', but it is a drinking vessel; 'on' just places one piece after the other. A beck is a stream in northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: John Steinbeck was the American novelist of The Grapes of Wrath and Of Mice and Men.
